The purpose of this policy is to define Cirque Corporation’s standardized process for the termination of employees, contractors, and temporary personnel to ensure the orderly separation of individuals from the organization while protecting company assets, information, and systems. This process supports the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and aligns with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clauses 6.3, 7.5, and Annex A controls related to human resource security and access management.

This policy applies to all Cirque Corporation personnel, including full-time employees, part-time employees, contractors, consultants, and temporary workers, across all global operations (US, Taipei, China). It covers voluntary and involuntary terminations, role separations, and contract expirations.

a. All terminations shall be handled in a consistent, professional, and legally compliant manner.
b. Termination activities shall be coordinated between Human Resources (HR), Information Technology (IT), the employee’s manager, and other relevant stakeholders.
c. Termination actions shall be executed promptly to minimize operational and information security risks.
a. HR shall formally initiate the termination process upon approval from authorized management.
b. IT and relevant process owners shall be notified in advance of the termination date when feasible, or immediately in cases of involuntary or high-risk terminations.
c. The termination date and time shall be clearly communicated to all responsible parties.
a. All logical access rights (e.g., network accounts, email, VPN, cloud services, applications) shall be disabled or revoked no later than the effective termination date and time.
b. Physical access (e.g., badges, keys, facility access) shall be revoked concurrently with logical access.
c. Privileged or administrative access shall be revoked immediately upon termination notification.
a. All company assets issued to the individual shall be identified, collected, and accounted for, including but not limited to laptops, mobile devices, ID badges, documents, and storage media.
b. Confidential information, intellectual property, and proprietary materials shall be returned or securely retained by Cirque Corporation.
c. Any data stored on personal or third-party devices (if permitted) shall be returned or securely removed in accordance with company policy.

b. HR may conduct an exit interview to gather feedback and reinforce ongoing confidentiality obligations.
c. Continuing obligations related to confidentiality, intellectual property, and non-disclosure agreements shall be reaffirmed to the departing individual.
